newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Vishay says decision to cancel Israel plant final.
newsitem.headline: Vishay says decision to cancel Israel plant final.

text.p: Vishay Intertechnology's decision to cancel plans for a $50 million plant in the Israeli town of Ofakim is final, despite a plea by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu to reconsider, a company spokesman said.
At a meeting between Vishay president Felix Zandman and Netanyahu on Tuesday, the prime minister requested the company reconsider its decision to cancel the plant.
Ofakim is a development town with one of the highest rates of unemployment in the country.
Zandman promised he would look into the matter but after the meeting Vishay directors decided they would stand by their earlier decision, the spokesman said on Wednesday.
Zandman, however, promised the company would do its best to employ hundreds of workers from Ofakim at its plant in Beersheba.
The Beersheba plant, Vishay's fifth in Israel, currently employs 400 workers but will soon reach a capacity of 1,000.
Vishay, a Pennsylvania-based maker of electronic components, cancelled its plans for the Ofakim plant following what it called bureaucratic delays in getting a government subsidy for the plant.

Israel's Investment Centre had informed Vishay it could not approve the project this year because it had exhausted its budget. Next year the maximum grant is due to fall to 20 percent from 34 percent this year.
